office_does: One of three members of the San Juan County Council, which adopts the county budget and sets policy; the member must live in District 3 (Lopez, Shaw, Decatur and nearby islands), but every county voter votes for the seat.
race_blurb: Open seat decided under a $3.7 million budget gap after voters rejected the county levy lid lift in April. Shaw Island's Jennifer Swanson, a former school board director and superintendent, pledges restraint; Lopez Island's Katherine Bryant Ingman, a nonprofit leader, would protect frontline services and names new revenue sources.

candidates.summary: Former Shaw Island school board director and superintendent who chairs the county Ferry Advisory Committee and co-founded the Shaw Island Community Land Trust; running on budget restraint, housing, ferries and the environment.
highlights: 11 years an elected school board director and 7 years superintendent on Shaw Island [S1]
"This is not the time to expand county services"; will "live within our means" and rebuild reserves [S4][S5]
Promises to look for "alternative ways the county can increase revenue" for 2028, without naming a tax [S5]
Co-founded the Shaw Island Community Land Trust; backs affordable housing "for the full income diversity of our county" [S3][S4]
Led the August primary with 2,944 votes [S9]

experience.basis: 11 years of elected school board service and 7 as superintendent; calls herself 'the longest track record and ... most experienced, seasoned candidate' who can 'hit the ground running', though she has not held county office.

spending.basis: Repeatedly pledges restraint: 'not the time to expand county services', 'live within our means', rebuild emergency reserves, seek efficiency, while protecting mandated and priority services.

taxes.basis: Reads the levy defeat as voters not wanting higher property taxes, yet commits to look for alternative county revenue for 2028; names no tax to add or cut.

housing.basis: Co-founded a community land trust and raises money for teacher housing; would advocate affordable housing for the full income range, alongside code revisions to ease affordable development.

climate.basis: Calls environmental protection 'of the utmost importance' given climate change impacts on the islands and took part in the county Climate Convergence; no energy-cost tradeoff stated.

candidates.summary: Lopez Island nonprofit leader (Washington Women's Foundation; president of the Catherine Washburn Medical Association) running for a first office on healthcare, housing, ferries, the environment and protecting frontline services.
highlights: Led the Lopez Clinic's transition to a new provider as president of the Catherine Washburn Medical Association [S5][S7][S9]
Would protect frontline services and infrastructure, reviewing management costs before cuts, and keep funding the county Home Fund [S5]
Names revenue tools: updated lodging taxes, short-term rental permitting, a 0.1% law-and-justice sales tax, voluntary visitor taxes [S5]
Wants the county Climate Action Plan integrated across departments [S4]
Has not held elected office; stresses a younger generation's stake [S1][S9]

experience.basis: No elected experience; argues 'with age doesn't always come more experience – sometimes we need to shake things up' and that her generation's perspective belongs at the table, while citing a decade of nonprofit leadership.

spending.basis: Would protect frontline services, invest in maintenance now and keep funding the Home Fund 'before cutting deeper', while reviewing administrative costs first and backing balanced budgets.

taxes.basis: Proposes new county revenue (updated lodging taxes, a 0.1% law-and-justice sales tax, visitor taxes) and was disappointed the levy lid lift failed, while ruling out asking islanders 'to shoulder more'.

housing.basis: Pairs public investment (protect and fund the county Home Fund, low- and moderate-income housing) with supply-side tools (ADU reforms, pre-approved plans, permit streamlining).

climate.basis: Would integrate the county Climate Action Plan across departments, build climate resilience and encourage on-island EV use.
